claims.text: Machine-learning-based interatomic potentials can improve the representation of atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation of atomic configurations leads to better reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved representation of atomic configurations reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method is applicable to both solid and liquid states at or near high melting temperatures.
Multicomponent high-entropy alloys contain complex atomic configurations relevant to the reference-potential problem.
Machine-learning-based interatomic potentials provide enhanced potential functions that capture many-body interactions.
Machine-learning-based references will improve phase-space overlap relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Machine-learning-based references will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
TOR-TILD uses EAM reference potentials as the relevant baseline.
